data.content:
Book
A book is an item that can be borrowed and should be returned on or before its due date.<SEP>The book is the borrowed item that may be renewed or returned.<SEP>A book is an item that can be borrowed, returned by its due date, and renewed if it is not reserved.<SEP>The Book is the borrowed item that may be renewed if nobody else has reserved it.<SEP>A book is an item students may borrow, renew, and return.

Renewal
Renewal is the process described for extending a book's loan when nobody else has reserved it.<SEP>A renewal extends the borrowing period once by seven days when nobody else has reserved the book.<SEP>Renewal is the process of extending a book loan once for seven extra days when no other borrower has reserved the book.

Reservation
A reservation determines whether the book can be renewed or must be returned by its original due date.<SEP>A reservation by another person prevents the described one-time, seven-day renewal.<SEP>A Reservation is another borrower's claim on a book and prevents renewal under the described instructions.

Page 2 of 2
The text displays “2 / 2,” indicating the second page of two.

Library Borrowing Guide
A guide titled “Library Borrowing Guide.”<SEP>The Library Borrowing Guide provides instructions about borrowing and returning books, account eligibility, loan limits, loan periods, and due dates.<SEP>The Library Borrowing Guide provides instructions for renewing and returning a borrowed book.<SEP>The Library Borrowing Guide provides instructions for checking titles, returning books, and renewing loans.<SEP>The Library Borrowing Guide provides instructions for renewing a borrowed book and handling a reservation.<SEP>The Library Borrowing Guide presents baseline borrowing rules and instructions for students.

Date
A date is mentioned as something to check again.

Due Date
A due date is the date by which each borrowed book should be returned.<SEP>The due date is the deadline by which a borrowed book should be returned and before which a renewal should be requested.<SEP>A due date is the date by which a borrowed book must be returned unless an eligible renewal applies.

My Loans
My Loans is the location where the new due date appears after renewal.<SEP>My Loans shows the due date for each borrowed book.<SEP>My Loans is the interface where a borrower can find a book and select the Renew option.<SEP>My Loans is a library account area where a borrower can find a book and view its updated due date.<SEP>My Loans is the account feature students use to check the due date for each title.

Loan Limit
The loan limit is listed in a table in the guide.

Title
A title identifies a book and should be checked separately according to the guide.

Borrowing And Returning Books
Borrowing and returning books are the activities covered by the Library Borrowing Guide.

Library Account Eligibility
Library account eligibility should be checked before borrowing.

Seven Extra Days
Seven extra days is the loan extension available for a renewal.<SEP>Seven extra days is the additional borrowing period allowed by an eligible renewal.

Standard Loan Period
The standard loan period is listed in a table in the guide.<SEP>The standard loan period is the baseline duration for borrowing a book.

Result Confirmation
Result confirmation is the instruction to verify the outcome of a renewal.

Renewal Steps
Renewal Steps is the caption of Figure 1, which presents steps for renewing a book.

New Due Date
The new due date is displayed in My Loans after a book is renewed.<SEP>The New Due Date is the updated deadline shown in My Loans after a successful renewal.

Loan Information Table
The table lists the loan limit and standard loan period.

Original Due Date
The original due date is the deadline for returning a reserved book.<SEP>The Original Due Date is the deadline by which a reserved book should be returned.

data.entity_name: Student Book Borrowing Limits and Standard Loan Period (table)
data.content: The table states that students may borrow a maximum of 3 books at a time and that the standard loan period is 14 days. It supplies the baseline rules for the surrounding guidance on checking each book’s due date, returning books on time, and conditionally renewing once for 7 extra days when no other borrower has reserved the book.

A three-step horizontal flowchart for renewing a library book: check the due date, find the book in My Loans, and renew it while checking the new due date. In the surrounding guide, renewal must be requested before the due date; eligibility and the updated due date should be checked.

Student
A student is subject to the borrowing limits and procedures described in the guide.

3 Books
Three books is the maximum number a student may borrow at one time.

14 Days
Fourteen days is the standard loan period for a borrowed book.

Maximum Books at a Time
The maximum books at a time rule sets the quantity of books a student may borrow simultaneously.

Student Account Eligibility
Student account eligibility is a condition students are instructed to check before borrowing.

Book Reservation
A reservation by another person prevents a student from renewing a book and requires return by the original due date.

7 Extra Days
Seven extra days is the duration of the permitted renewal extension.

Renewal Rule
The renewal rule allows a student to renew a book once for an extra seven days before its due date, provided nobody else has reserved it.

Before the Due Date
Before the Due Date is the time by which a borrower is instructed to check the loan and request a renewal.

Renew Command
The Renew Command is the interface option the borrower clicks to request a book renewal.

Renewal Steps Flowchart
The Renewal Steps Flowchart visually summarizes checking the due date, finding the book in My Loans, renewing it, and checking the updated due date.
